description: August 15, 2021. Kabul falls to the Taliban in hours, not the weeks the CIA had predicted. President Ashraf Ghani flees. The US-trained 300,000-man Afghan National Army collapses without a fight. India had invested $3 billion in Afghanistan — Salma Dam, Kandahar consulates, Parliament building, roads — all now under Taliban control. India had 4 consulates in Afghanistan, all closed in panic. NSA Ajay Sanyal must perform an immediate strategic recalibration: Pakistan's 'strategic depth' in Afghanistan is now realised, but its costs are also visible — the TTP (Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan) will be emboldened, Pakistan's western border will bleed. The key intelligence question: will the Taliban honour the Pakistan-ISI relationship that gave it sanctuary for 20 years, or will the Pashtunwali code and TTP pressures turn Afghanistan into Pakistan's own strategic nightmare?

real_world_correlation.real_event: Taliban captured Kabul August 15, 2021 — ahead of the September 11 US withdrawal deadline. President Ghani fled to UAE with cash-filled helicopters (disputed). ANA collapse: 300,000 trained soldiers, $88 billion in US military equipment, yielded without sustained resistance. Taliban took 33 of 34 provincial capitals in 10 days. India evacuated its ambassador and staff from Kabul; closed Kandahar, Herat, Jalalabad, and Mazar-i-Sharif consulates.
real_world_correlation.india_investment_lost: India's $3 billion investment in Afghanistan — including the $290m Salma Dam (renamed Afghan-India Friendship Dam), Kabul Parliament Building ($90m), Zaranj-Delaram highway (218km, connecting Afghan road network to Iran border), multiple consulates — all fell under Taliban control. India had no Taliban relationship to leverage.
real_world_correlation.pakistan_strategic_depth_costs: ISI's long-term strategy of supporting the Taliban as 'strategic depth' against India succeeded in its immediate objective — but at unexpected costs: (1) TTP (Pakistani Taliban), emboldened by Afghan Taliban success, dramatically escalated attacks inside Pakistan from 2021 onward; (2) Afghanistan under Taliban refused to honour the Durand Line; (3) Afghan Taliban-ISI relations deteriorated over Pakistan's treatment of Afghan refugees and TTP sanctuary
real_world_correlation.ttp_escalation: TTP attacks inside Pakistan: 2021 — 300+ attacks; 2022 — 500+; 2023 — 700+; 2024 — 900+. Pakistan's own 'strategic asset' (Afghan Taliban) was enabling Pakistan's worst terrorist threat (TTP). The chickens-coming-home dynamic Sanyal would monologue about.
real_world_correlation.india_quiet_engagement: Despite having no consular presence, India quietly re-engaged with the Taliban through back-channels by 2023. Indian technical staff resumed work on Salma Dam. Trade through Pakistan-India was explored for Afghan access. India's pragmatic engagement with the Taliban (without recognition) was classic NSA Doval doctrine — interests over ideology.
real_world_correlation.raw_intelligence_failure: RAW's assessment of ANA collapse timeline was significantly wrong. US CIA's 'months not weeks' prediction was also wrong. The speed of Taliban advance caught every intelligence agency off-guard — representing a fundamental failure to assess the ANA's will to fight vs. its equipment capability.

mission_tasks.name: Assess whether Taliban will honour ISI relationship or use strategic independence now that US is gone
Map TTP escalation trajectory post-Kabul — assess when TTP instability becomes strategic opportunity for India (Pakistan two-front internal)
Assess ISI's intent to use Afghan territory as a safe staging area for operations against India under Taliban cover
Assess Taliban's real military capability from US equipment windfall — helicopters, armoured vehicles, night vision — impact on ISI's proxy capability

adversaries.objective: Maintain Taliban relationship and extract strategic benefit from Kabul; use Afghan territory for anti-India operations; manage TTP threat to Pakistan's own stability; prevent India from re-establishing Afghan presence
Establish governance; manage TTP relationship; extract economic resources from all international actors including India; avoid being constrained solely by Pakistan

intelligence_targets.name: Whether Taliban is providing ISI operational space for anti-India activities in Afghan territory post-Kabul
TTP attack trajectory — when does TTP destabilisation of Pakistan create a strategic opening for India to apply pressure
Degree of Taliban openness to quiet Indian engagement — trade, technical assistance, Salma Dam — without formal recognition
